text: In the twenty-second chapter of Genesis a question is left which receives no answer. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; yet of what he feels nothing is told, and the narrator never opens his inward life. He makes no protest; he enters into no bargain. The man who pleaded for Sodom is absent here. Abraham, in Genesis 22, appears less as a character than as a silence, and the whole chapter turns upon the silence of Abraham.
